tasks.description: Implement src/lru.js exporting class `LruCache` with constructor `new LruCache({ max, ttlMs = Infinity, now = Date.now })`. Methods: `get(key)` returns the value or undefined (an expired entry counts as missing and is removed; a hit makes the key most recently used), `set(key, value, { ttlMs } = {})` inserts/updates (updating makes it most recently used; a per-entry ttlMs overrides the default; when over `max`, evict least recently used entries, preferring to evict expired entries first), `has(key)` (like get but does not change recency), `delete(key)` returns boolean, `size` getter counting only non-expired entries, and `keys()` returning non-expired keys from least to most recently used. get, set, has and delete must be O(1) amortised: with no expiring entries the cache must handle 60k get/set calls at max 20000 in well under a second (scanning for expired entries is only acceptable when some entry has a finite TTL). `now` is injectable for tests. Write your own tests in test/ and run them with `node --test` (it finds test/*.test.mjs; on Node 24 `node --test test/` fails because a directory argument is not accepted).

Implement src/limiter.js exporting `createLimiter({ capacity, refillPerSec, now = Date.now })`, a per-key token-bucket rate limiter. It returns `{ take(key, cost = 1), peek(key) }`. Each key starts with a full bucket of `capacity` tokens and refills continuously at `refillPerSec` tokens per second (fractional refill allowed, never above capacity). `take` returns `{ ok: true, remaining }` and consumes `cost` tokens when enough are available, otherwise `{ ok: false, remaining, retryAfterMs }` without consuming anything, where retryAfterMs is the whole number of milliseconds (rounded up) until enough tokens will be available. `cost` greater than capacity always fails with `retryAfterMs: Infinity`. `remaining` is the number of tokens left, rounded down to an integer. `peek(key)` returns the current token count (rounded down) without consuming. Time comes only from `now()` (milliseconds). Write your own tests in test/ and run `node --test` (it finds test/*.test.mjs; on Node 24 `node --test test/` fails because a directory argument is not accepted).

`mapLimit(items, limit, fn)` in src/map-limit.js should run the async `fn(item, index)` over items with at most `limit` calls in flight at any time, resolve to the results in input order, and reject with the first error as soon as any call rejects (starting no new calls after that). The test in test/ is flaky and users report results in the wrong order, more than `limit` calls running at once, and the promise never settling for empty input. Find the root causes and fix them. Run `node --test` (it finds test/*.test.mjs; on Node 24 `node --test test/` fails because a directory argument is not accepted) several times.

Implement src/expr.js exporting `evaluate(source, vars = {})` for a small arithmetic language, without using eval or Function. Numbers (integers and decimals like 2.5 or .5), variables (identifiers [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*, looked up in vars; an unknown variable throws Error `unknown variable: <name>`), binary + - * / % and ^ (power, right-associative, binds tighter than unary minus so -2^2 is -4), unary minus and plus, parentheses, and whitespace anywhere. Usual precedence: ^ above unary minus above * / % above + -; * / % + - are left-associative. Division by zero throws Error `division by zero`. Any syntax error throws an Error whose message starts with `syntax error`. Write your own tests in test/ and run `node --test` (it finds test/*.test.mjs; on Node 24 `node --test test/` fails because a directory argument is not accepted).

Implement src/resolve.js exporting `resolveOrder(packages, targets)`. `packages` maps a name to `{ deps: string[] }`; `targets` is an array of names to install. Return the install order: every needed package (targets and their transitive deps, each once) such that each package comes after all of its deps. Among packages whose deps are all already placed, always pick the alphabetically smallest next (so the order is deterministic). A dependency that is not in `packages` throws Error `missing package: <name> (required by <parent>)` (for a missing target: `missing package: <name> (required by <root>)`). A cycle throws Error `cycle: a -> b -> a` naming the cycle as found by a depth-first search that visits targets in the given order and deps in their listed order, starting the path at the first package of the cycle. Packages not needed by the targets must not appear. Create src/ranges.js exporting `mergeRanges(ranges)`.

`ranges` is an array of [start, end] pairs of integers, both ends inclusive. Return a new array of merged [start, end] pairs sorted by start.
- Two ranges merge when they overlap OR when they touch, i.e. the next start is at most the current end + 1. Example: [[1,3],[4,6]] becomes [[1,6]].
- A range fully inside another is absorbed. The merged end is the larger of the two ends.
- The input must not be mutated, and every returned pair must be a fresh array.
- An empty input returns [].
- If any pair has start > end, throw a RangeError whose message is `bad range: ` followed by JSON.stringify of that pair, e.g. `bad range: [5,2]`.

Before you finish, run `node check.mjs` in the work folder; it must pass. Reply with one short line saying what you did.

Create src/limiter.js exporting `createLimiter(max)`. It returns a function `run(fn)`.

- `createLimiter(max)` throws a RangeError with message `max must be a positive integer` unless max is an integer >= 1.
- `run(fn)` returns a Promise that resolves to fn's return value (awaiting it if fn returns a promise), or rejects with the error fn throws or rejects with.
- At most `max` jobs are running at any moment. Other jobs wait in a first-in first-out queue and start in the order they were submitted.
- fn is called with no arguments, and never synchronously inside the `run(fn)` call: it starts on a later tick.
- A job that throws synchronously, or whose promise rejects, still frees its slot so the queue keeps moving.

Before you finish, run `node check.mjs` in the work folder; it must pass. Reply with one short line saying what you did.

Create src/template.js exporting `render(template, vars)`, a small placeholder renderer.

- A placeholder is `{{name}}`, where name is an identifier (letters, digits, underscore, not starting with a digit). Spaces just inside the braces are allowed: `{{ name }}` is the same placeholder.
- Each placeholder is replaced with String(vars[name]). A value is inserted exactly as it is: `$&`, `$1` and similar text in a value stay as literal text, and values are never scanned for placeholders again.
- A value that is 0, '', false or null is rendered as its String form ("0", "", "false", "null"). Only a name that is missing from vars (not an own property) counts as missing.
- If a placeholder names a missing variable, throw an Error with message `missing variable: ` followed by the name. If several are missing, report the first one in template order.
- Anything that is not a placeholder, including single braces like `{x}`, is copied unchanged.

Before you finish, run `node check.mjs` in the work folder; it must pass. Reply with one short line saying what you did.

Create src/csv.js exporting `parseCsv(text)`, which returns an array of rows, each row an array of string fields.

- Fields are separated by commas. Records end at LF or CRLF.
- A field wrapped in double quotes may contain commas, LF and CR characters, and a doubled quote (two double-quote characters in a row) that stands for one literal quote. Quotes inside an unquoted field are literal characters.
- A single LF or CRLF at the very end of the input does not start an extra record. An empty line in the middle is a record with one empty field: the input "a", LF, LF, "b" gives [["a"],[""],["b"]].
- An empty input string returns []. The input of two double quotes alone (a quoted empty field) returns [[""]].
- If the input ends inside a quoted field, throw an Error with message `unterminated quoted field`.

Create src/pages.js exporting `pageWindow(total, page, perPage, span)`. It returns the page numbers a pager should show.

- `total` is a non-negative integer item count, `perPage` an integer >= 1, `span` an integer >= 1 (the most page links to show).
- totalPages = max(1, ceil(total / perPage)). `page` must be an integer from 1 to totalPages; otherwise throw a RangeError with message `page out of range: ` followed by the page value, e.g. `page out of range: 11`.
- Let len = min(span, totalPages). The window is len consecutive page numbers that contain `page`, centred so that floor(span / 2) pages come before `page` when there is room (for an even span the extra link goes after the current page).
- Clamp the window to the pages that exist: it never starts below 1 and never ends above totalPages.
- Return the page numbers as an array of integers in ascending order.

Examples: pageWindow(100, 5, 10, 5) gives [3,4,5,6,7]; pageWindow(100, 1, 10, 4) gives [1,2,3,4].

Before you finish, run `node check.mjs` in the work folder; it must pass. Reply with one short line saying what you did.
